sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner/accused No.1 under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for granting regular bail in respect of Crime No.341/2023 registered by Byadarahalli Police for the offenses punishable under Sections 498A, 307, 323 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent-State.
3.

The case of the prosecution is that on the complaint of Tejaswini/defacto complainant, wife of the petitioner/accused No.1 on 13.06.2023 alleging that the marriage of the petitioner and respondent was solemnized on 06.11.2022 and at the time of marriage, the petitioner had demanded and accepted 40 gms. of gold, 1 Kg. Silver articles and cash of Rs.50,000/-.
Subsequently suspecting the fidelity, the petitioner quarreling with the complainant NC: 2023:KHC:25408 and demanding Rs.20,00,000/- and also demanding her salary.
There was quarrel on 14.04.2023 at about 11.00 p.m., and a Panchayat was held and complainant was sent back to the petitioner.

On 11.06.2023,
once again the petitioner said to have picked up quarrel and tried to strangulate the victim, however,
she escaped and locked the room and telephoned to her mother.
Accordingly, her relatives came and rescued her.
4. After registering the case, the Police arrested the petitioner on 13.06.2023.
His bail petition came to be rejected and therefore, the petitioner is before this Court.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted prior to that, the mother of the petitioner had complained against the complainant family members which was registered subsequent to registering FIR in Crime No.347/2023 at 9.30 p.m. Infact the mother of the complainant filed first complaint.
Then the Police called all the persons to the Police Station and obtained the complaint of the complainant and registered FIR.
Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader resisted the bail petition and prays to reject the bail petition.

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances, the alleged offense is not punishable with death or imprisonment and there is no serious injury sustained by the defacto complainant.
The accused said to have attempted to strangulate the defacto complainant and he is in custody for almost more than one month.
The co- accused persons were already granted bail by the trial Court.

Considering the same, I am of the view that by imposing certain conditions, if the petitioner/accused is granted bail,
no prejudice would be caused to the case of the prosecution.
Hence, the criminal petition is allowed.

Sd/-
